Rashi on Sukkah 34b:1:1.hebrew: לגיטי נשים - דקיימא לן (גיטין דף ב.): המביא גט מחוצה לארץ צריך שיאמר ״בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם״ — אי משום דאין מצויין לקיימו, ואי משום דאין בקיאין לשמה; והמביא מארץ ישראל אינו צריך, לפי שבקיאין לשמה, ועולי רגלים מצויין להכיר חתימת עדים לקיימו. ואמרי' התם (דף ו.): ״בבל כארץ ישראל לגיטין״, לפי שהן בני תורה ובקיאין לשמה, ובני ישיבה מצויין לילך וללמוד משם תורה מכל מקומות. ובורסיף סמוך לבבל ואינן בני תורה, כדאמרינן (סנהדרין דף קט.): ״מאי בורסיף? בור ששפו את מימיו ולא נשתייר בו כלום״, והמביא משם צריך שיאמר. אבל עכשיו נתחלף שמם. הלכך, המביא מבבל צריך שיאמר, ומבורסיף אין צריך:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:1:1.english: For women’s bills of divorce - For we maintain (Gittin 2a) that one who brings a bill of divorce from outside the Land of Israel must say: “In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed,” whether because [people] are not commonly available to ratify it, or because they are not experts [in writing it] for its own sake; whereas one who brings [it] from the Land of Israel does not need [to say this], because they are experts [in writing it] for its own sake and festival pilgrims are commonly available to recognize the witnesses’ signatures to ratify it. And we say there (6a): “Babylon is like the Land of Israel with regard to bills of divorce,” because they are people of Torah and are experts [in writing it] for its own sake, and yeshiva students are commonly available to go and learn Torah there from all places. And Borsif is near Babylon, and they are not people of Torah, as we say (Sanhedrin 109a): “What is [the meaning of] Borsif? A pit whose water has been drained and nothing remained in it”; and one who brings [a bill of divorce] from there must say [the declaration]. But now their names have been switched. Therefore, one who brings [a bill of divorce] from Babylon must say [it], and [one who brings it] from Borsif does not need [to say it].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:2:1.english: Three myrtle branches - In the Gemara, it derives this.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:2:2.hebrew: ואפילו שנים קטומין - אהדסים קאי. ובגמרא פריך: מה נפשך? אי קטום פסול, והוא צריך שלשה — ליבעי כולהו שלימים! ואי קטום כשר — לכשיר שלשתן קטומים! ומשני: חזר בו ר' ישמעאל מתחלת דבריו שהיה מצריך שלשה, ואמר אפי' שנים קטומין — והוא הדין אי לא מייתי להו לגמרי, דהא קטומים כמאן דליתנהו דמי:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:2:2.english: And even if two are severed - This refers to the myrtle branches. And in the Gemara, it asks: Whichever way you look at it: if a severed [myrtle] is invalid and he requires three, let him require all of them [to be] whole; and if a severed [myrtle] is valid, let him validate [even if] all three of them are severed! And [the Gemara] answers: Rabbi Yishmael retracted his initial statement in which he required three, and said “even [if] two are severed” — and the same applies if he did not bring them at all, for severed [branches] are considered as though they do not exist.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:2:3.hebrew: ר' טרפון אומר אפי' שלשתן קטומים - דלא בעי הדר בהדס:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:2:3.english: Rabbi Tarfon says: Even if all three of them are severed - For he does not require beauty in a myrtle [branch].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:3:1.english: “Branches of a date palm” [is] one - This implies that it is written kappat [without a vav].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:3:2.hebrew: ענף - חד, עץ — חד, עבות — חד:

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:3:3.english: And even if two are severed - It refers to the myrtle.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:4:1.hebrew: יכול יאגדם כולן - ואף האתרוג עמהם? אמרת: וכי נאמר "וכפת תמרים", דניהוי משמע וי"ו מוסיף על ענין ראשון לצרפו עם "פרי עץ הדר"? והלא לא נאמר אלא "כפת", משמע בפני עצמן הן, ולא עם האתרוג. "וענף עץ" מוסיף עליהם, "וערבי נחל" מוסיף עליהם, שנאמר בהן ווי"ן — לפיכך נאגדין עם הלולב:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:4:1.english: I might [think] he should bind them all - And even the etrog with them? You say: Was it stated, "and branches of palm trees," so that the vav would imply adding to the first subject, to join it with "the fruit of a beautiful tree"? But surely it was only stated "branches," which implies that they are on their own, and not with the etrog. And "a bough of a [dense-leaved] tree" adds to them, and "willows of the brook" adds to them, as vavs are stated regarding them; therefore, they are bound with the lulav.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:4:2.hebrew: שמעכבין זה את זה - אם חסר אחת מארבעתן, אין השלשה מצוה:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:4:2.english: That they are mutually indispensable - If one of the four of them is missing, the [remaining] three are not a mitzvah.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:4:3.english: Complete - Whole; for he expounds [the word ulkaḥtem as]: A complete taking [ulkaḥat tam].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:5:1.hebrew: ור' ישמעאל - דמכשיר שנים קטומים וחד מצריך שלם — היכן חלקן הכתוב? אי בעי הדר — ניבעי בכולהו, ואי לא בעי הדר — אפילו בחד לא נצריך:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:5:1.english: And Rabbi Yishmael - Who validates two severed [myrtle branches] and requires one [to be] whole — where did Scripture distinguish between them? If he requires beauty [hadar], let him require [it] for all of them; and if he does not require beauty, even for one let us not require [it].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:5:2.english: Bira'a said - The name of a Sage.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:5:3.hebrew: חזר בו ר' ישמעאל - מתחלת דבריו, ומכשר בחד, ומיהו הדר בעי:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:5:3.english: Rabbi Yishmael retracted [his statement] - [He retracted] from his initial statement, and he deems [it] valid with one [myrtle branch]; but nevertheless, he requires beauty [i.e., that it be whole].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:6:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' טרפון - להקל, דקטום כשר:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:6:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon - To be lenient, [ruling] that a severed [myrtle branch] is fit.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:6:2.hebrew: אשוו וזבינו - מכרו בשוה, ואל תעלו על דמיהם, מפני שמבקשים מכם שלשה הדסין ושלמים:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:6:2.english: Equate and sell - Sell at a fair price, and do not raise their prices because they ask of you three whole myrtle branches.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:6:3.english: And if not - [That is, if] you do not set a fair price.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:6:4.english: I will teach in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon - For he deems severed [myrtles] fit.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:7:1.hebrew: כר"ע - דלא בעי אלא חד:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:7:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Akiva - As he requires only one [myrtle branch].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:8:1.english: [An etrog] of orla and of impure teruma is unfit - In the Gemara, the reason is explained.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:8:2.english: One may not take [it] - In the Gemara, it explains the reason.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:8:3.english: In Jerusalem - For it is fit for the consumption of second tithe.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:8:4.english: One may not take [it] - As is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:8:5.hebrew: ואם נטל כשר - שהרי יש בה היתר אכילה, אבל חוץ לירושלים לא, ד"לכם" כתיב — הראוי לכם:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:8:5.english: And if one took it, it is fit - For there is permission to eat it [in Jerusalem]; but outside of Jerusalem, [it is] not [fit], for it is written: "For you" (Leviticus 23:40) — [meaning,] that which is suitable for you [to eat].

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:1.english: A boil-like blemish - A kind of small blisters.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:2.hebrew: נטלה פטמתו - ראש אתרוג, מפי רבי' יעקב. ודוגמתו: הפטמ' של רמון (עוקצין פ"ב מ"ג):
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:2.english: [If] its protuberance was removed - The top of the etrog, [as heard] from the mouth of Rabbeinu Yaakov. And an example of it [is]: “The protuberance of a pomegranate” (Uktzin 2:3).

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:3.hebrew: הכי גרסי': נקלף, נסדק, ניקב וחסר כל שהוא — פסול - "ניקב וחסר כל שהוא" חדא מילתא, דאילו ניקב ולא חסר — שתחב בו מחט והוציאה — כשר, כדקתני סיפא:
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:3.english: This is the text we read: [If it] was peeled, split, [or] pierced and missing any amount, [it is] unfit - “Pierced and missing any amount” is one [single] matter; for if it was pierced and was not missing [anything] — [such as] where one stuck a needle into it and removed it — [it is] fit, as it teaches in the latter clause.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:4.hebrew: ניטל עוקצו - זנבו, כמו בעוקצי תאנים (סנהדרין דף מ.):
Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:4.english: [If] its stem was removed - Its tail [i.e., its stalk], as in "with the stems of figs" (Sanhedrin 40a).

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:5.english: The Cushite - That came from the land of Cush, and it is black.

Rashi on Sukkah 34b:9:7.english: And in a large [one] - That it should not be excessively large.

Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:1:1.hebrew: נפקא מינה לגיטי נשים - כדפירש בקונט': דקיימא לן בפ"ק דגיטין (דף ו.) דבבל כארץ ישראל לגיטין — דאין צריך לומר "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם", דשכיחי מתיבתא ובקיאין לשמה, וגם עדים מצויין לקיימו; והיינו מה שקורין בורסיף, דמשתני שמה. ובסוף במה מדליקין (שבת דף לו: ושם) פי' עוד לשון אחר: ונפקא מינה לענין שמו ושמה ושם עירו ושם עירה. ולא יתכן; דבבל הוא שם המדינה, כדאמר (קדושין דף עא.): "א"י עיסה לבבל", ואמרי' פרק עשרה יוחסין (שם): "עד היכן הוא בבל?" — ואין כותבין שם המדינה בגט, אלא שם העיר:
Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:1:1.english: A practical difference for women's bills of divorce - As explained in the Kuntres [by Rashi]: For we maintain in the first chapter of Gittin (6a) that Babylonia is like Eretz Yisrael regarding bills of divorce — that [the bearer] does not need to say, "In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed," because academies [of Torah] are prevalent [there] and they are knowledgeable [that a get must be written] for her sake, and witnesses are also readily available to ratify it; and this [rule] applies to that which [people now] call Bursif, as its name was changed. And at the end of [the chapter] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 36b, and see there), he explained yet another phrasing: that a practical difference emerges regarding [the law of one who changed] his name and her name, or the name of his city and the name of her city. But this cannot be, for Babylonia is the name of the province, as it says (Kiddushin 71a): "Eretz Yisrael is [like mixed] dough compared to Babylonia," and we say in chapter Asarah Yuchasin (ibid.): "How far does Babylonia extend?" — and they do not write the name of the province in a bill of divorce, but rather the name of the city.

Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:3:1.hebrew: ענף עץ עבות שלשה - פי' בקונט': ענף — חד, עץ — חד, עבות — חד. ותימה, דלעיל (סוכה דף לב:) אוקימנא: "ענף עץ" — שענפיו חופין את עציו, ודרשינן נמי: "עץ עבות" — קלוע כמין קליעה! וא"ת: ונימא "פרי עץ הדר" — שלשה? וי"ל: דמדרשא דעץ דרשינן, שטעם עצו ופריו שוים:
Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:3:1.english: "Boughs of a dense-leaved tree" [means] three - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: "Bough" [anaf] is one, "tree" [etz] is one, [and] "dense-leaved" [avot] is one. And it is astonishing, as earlier (Sukkah 32b) we established: "A bough of a tree" [means] that its branches cover its wood, and we also expounded: "A dense-leaved tree" [means that it is] braided like a braid! And if you say: then let us say [that] "the fruit of a beautiful tree" [indicates] three? One can say: from the exposition of "tree" we expound that the taste of its wood and its fruit are identical.

Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:3:2.hebrew: ערבי נחל שתים - אפילו נותן כמה הדסים וכמה ערבות בלולב, אין זה בל תוסיף, אפילו למ"ד צריך אגד, אא"כ מוסיף מין אחר — כדפרישית בסוף ראוהו בית דין (ר"ה דף כח: ד"ה ומנא):
Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:3:2.english: "Willows of the brook: Two" - Even if one places several myrtle branches and several willow branches with the lulav, this is not [a violation of] "do not add" [bal tosif], even according to the one who says [that the four species] require binding, unless one adds another species — as I explained at the end of [the chapter] Ra'uhu Beit Din (Rosh Hashanah 28b, s.v. U-mena).

Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:4:1.hebrew: שתהא לקיחה תמה - מהאי טעמא נמי פסלינן אתרוג חסר, משום דאין זה לקיחה תמה. וביום שני לא חיישינן, אף על גב דקפדינן אארבעה מינין; וטעמא פירשתי בריש פירקין (סוכה דף כט: ושם ב"'ה בעינן). ובהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כז.) מסיק, דהא דמעכבי אהדדי — לא שנו אלא שאין לו, אבל יש לו — אין מעכבין. ופירש בהלכות גדולות: "אין מעכבין" — דלא תימא עד דמגבה להו בהדי הדדי, אלא אי מגבה כל חד וחד לחודיה שפיר דמי, דקיימא לן לולב אין צריך אגד. ודבר תימה הוא לומר כן, דכיון דכולו מצוה אחת — היאך יועילו בזה אחר זה?! ור״ת הגיה בספרו: לא שנו דמעכבין משום תמה אלא שאין לו, אבל יש לו — תמה הוא, אע״פ שלא חברו באגדו; כדאמרי' (לעיל סוכה דף לג.) דלא דרשי רבנן "לקיחה" "לקיחה", ולר' יהודה דדריש "לקיחה" — משמע ליה דלא הוי תמה אא״כ אגדו:
Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:4:1.english: "That it shall be a complete taking" - For this reason as well we disqualify a deficient etrog, because this is not a "complete taking." And on the second day [of the Festival], we are not concerned [about this], even though we are particular about [having all] four species; and the reason I explained at the beginning of our chapter (Sukkah 29b, and there in the comment beginning Ba'inan). And in [the chapter entitled] Hakometz Rabba (Menachot 27a), [the Gemara] concludes that this [ruling] that they are mutually indispensable was taught only when one does not have [all four]; but if one has [all four], they are not mutually indispensable. And [the author of] Halakhot Gedolot explained: "They are not mutually indispensable" — so that you should not say [one does not fulfill the mitzvah] until he lifts them up together; rather, if he lifts each one individually, it is fine, since we hold that the lulav does not require binding. And it is an astonishing thing to say so, for since it is all one mitzvah, how could they be effective one after another?! And Rabbeinu Tam emended [the text] in his book: They only taught that they are mutually indispensable due to [the requirement of a] "complete" [taking] when one does not have [all four]; but if one has [all four], it is [considered] "complete," even though he did not join them in its bundle — as we say (above, Sukkah 33a) that the Rabbis do not derive [the verbal analogy of] "taking" [and] "taking," whereas according to Rabbi Yehuda, who derives [it from] "taking," it implies to him that it is not "complete" unless he bound it.

Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:7:1.hebrew: ולדרוש להו כר"ע דמיקל טפי - תימה: הא לא סבירא ליה כר"ע, אלא כרבי טרפון! וי"ל, דכל זה מן הדיוק שבא להוכיח דשמואל לטעמי', דכרבי טרפון סבירא ליה: דאי מפחיד להו במידי דלא סבר כדי שימכרו בזול — היה לו להפחידם מר"ע דמיקל טפי. ודחי: אדרב', מפחדי טפי מרבי טרפון, דתלתא קטומין שכיחי מחד דלא קטים; ומעולם לא תשמע דסבר כרבי טרפון. ומיהו קשה מפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף ל.) מקדירות בפסח, דאמר שמואל: משהי להו עד אחר הפסח ועביד בהו בין במינו בין שלא במינו, ואמרינן: "ואזדא שמואל לטעמיה, דאמר להו שמואל להנהו דמזבנו כנדי: אשוו זבינייכו, ואי לא — דרישנא לכו כרבי שמעון", כלומר: דשרי חמץ לאחר הפסח כי ליתיה בעיניה; ומשמע בהדיא דלא מפחד במידי דלא סבר ליה! וי"ל: דהתם, למה לו להפחידם במידי דלא סבר ליה? דבשלמא הכא מצי למימר דהיה מפחידם כדי שימכרו בזול ותהא המצוה מצויה ולא ימנעו בשביל יוקר. וא"ת: ואי סבר לה כר' טרפון, לידרוש להו כוותיה? דכי האי גוונא פריך בפרק כל שעה (שם), ומשני: אתרי' דרב הוה. וי"ל, דהכא הניח משום הידור מצוה. ובריש בבא בתרא (דף ה. ושם) גבי רוניא, דאקפיה רבינא מארבע רוחותיו, ואתא לקמיה דרבא, ואמר: "זיל פייסיה במאי דאיפייס, ואי לא — דיינינא לך כרב הונא אליבא דרבי יוסי, דאמר: הכל לפי מה שגדר" — מה שלא דן לו, לפי שנתפייס רבינא ומחל לו בפחות:
Tosafot on Sukkah 34b:7:1.english: "And let him teach them in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who is even more lenient" - [This question is] astonishing: But he does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, only in accordance with Rabbi Tarfon! And one can say that all of this [question] stems from the inference that sought to prove that Shmuel conforms to his line of reasoning that he holds like Rabbi Tarfon: For if [it were so that] he was [merely] frightening them with something he does not hold in order that they would sell cheaply, he should have frightened them with [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva, who is even more lenient! And [the Gemara] rejects [this]: On the contrary, they are more frightened of [the ruling of] Rabbi Tarfon, as three severed [myrtles] are common, [whereas] one that is not severed is uncommon; and you would never deduce [from this threat] that he holds like Rabbi Tarfon. However, there is a difficulty from the chapter [entitled] "Kol Sha'ah" (Pesachim 30a) regarding pots on Passover, where Shmuel says: "One may keep them until after Passover and use them, whether [for food] of its kind or not of its kind"; and we say: "And Shmuel conforms to his line of reasoning, as Shmuel said to those who sell pots: 'Equate your prices, and if not, I will teach [the halakha] to you in accordance with Rabbi Shimon'" — that is to say, that he permits chametz after Passover when it is not substance itself — and this clearly implies that he would not frighten [people] with something he does not hold! And one can say: There, why should he frighten them with something he does not hold? For granted, here [one] can say that he was frightening them in order that they would sell cheaply, so that the mitzvah would be available and [people] would not refrain [from performing it] on account of high cost. And if you say: And if he holds like Rabbi Tarfon, let him teach [it to] them in accordance with his view? For in a similar manner [the Gemara] challenges in the chapter [entitled] "Kol Sha'ah" (ibid.) and answers: It was the locale of Rav. And one can say that here he refrained because of beautification of the mitzvah [hiddur mitzvah]. And at the beginning of Bava Batra (5a and there) regarding Ronya, whose [field] Ravina surrounded on four sides, and he came before Rava, and [Rava] said: "Go appease him with whatever he will be appeased with, and if not, I will judge you according to Rav Huna in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Yosei, who said: 'Everything is according to what he fenced'" — the reason he did not judge him [like Rav Huna immediately was] because Ravina was appeased and forgave him for less.
